key_insight: Embedding trained neural networks into optimization models can capture complex relationships, but smaller, sparser networks can make the resulting problems easier to solve.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can use learned constraints or objective approximations to model data-driven systems while balancing predictive fidelity against optimization cost.
method: Train neural networks to represent empirical constraints or approximate nonlinear objectives.
Embed the trained networks into an optimization model.
Consider smaller, sparser networks to improve computational tractability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a case study highlighting the benefit of smaller and sparser networks, without specifying datasets or quantitative results.
watch_item: Embedding neural networks can produce optimization models that are too large or too slow to solve.
paper_title: Constraint Learning by Optimizing over Trained Neural Networks: A Pragmatic Tutorial
